author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Alan Eyre, a former senior US diplomat who helped negotiate the 2015 Iran nuclear deal, joins Al Jazeera from Washington, DC, to assess the fallout from the US war with Iran. He says it has seriously damaged US soft power in the Gulf, pushing GCC states toward strategic hedging since Trump pursued the campaign unilaterally, turning "America First" into "America Alone."

Eyre says Washington has lost leverage on two fronts: having already used its military "stick" without forcing Iranian capitulation, and because Tehran no longer believes complying with US demands would ease pressure, seeing the real goal as regime change. Domestically, he says an unpopular war matters less to Trump than to a nervous Republican Party ahead of the midterms, with Trump focused on avoiding the appearance of a strategic blunder despite false claims that Iran will never get a nuclear weapon and that the Strait of Hormuz is open.

Asked whether this is heading toward a deal, Eyre predicts further escalation
title: Iran war has cost Washington leverage, Gulf trust, and any path to a quick end: Analysis

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The US military footprint across the Middle East has expanded to sustain the war with Iran, with roughly 50,000 troops now stationed in the region and two of America's three available aircraft carriers pulled from the Pacific.

The US operates 11 aircraft carriers, far more than any other country, but most sit at home at any given time. Three are currently deployed: the USS George Washington, redeployed from the Indo-Pacific, has joined the USS George H.W. Bush in the Arabian Sea, leaving no US carrier presence near China and its Pacific allies. The USS Abraham Lincoln has been deployed for more than 280 days and is finally heading home, with reports of food shortages and broken toilets and showers on board.

Each Nimitz-class carrier measures 332.9 metres and carries around 5,000 crew and roughly 70 aircraft, more than half of them fighter jets, putting significant firepower close to Iran. But the cost is real: right now, no US aircraft carrier is deployed anywhere else in the world.
title: The toll of stretching US aircraft carriers thin for the Iran war

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Gaza, seen through the legal and political framework of genocide, as allegations are argued in real time before international courts. 

This episode traces how decades of occupation, blockade and repeated wars created conditions of confinement, dependency and dehumanisation long before the war that began on October 7, 2023. It explores how displacement orders, siege tactics, destruction of infrastructure, and AI-assisted targeting have shaped the scale and pattern of killing and destruction. 

Drawing on testimony, military analysis and legal argument, the episode follows how Palestinian victims, Israel, and third states frame the intent and nature of the violence, and why the International Court of Justice has warned of a “plausible risk” of genocide without yet ruling on its commission. 

It asks what this unfolding legal battle means for accountability, future deterrence and the people of Gaza themselves.

#gaza #israel #palestine #documentary #artificialintelligence #aljazeeraengl

description:
Two days of Chile-US talks over new tariffs on Chilean exports have ended without a breakthrough.
Washington says negotiations will continue only if Chilean ministers stop publicly criticising the measures.
Chile disputes the US justification for an additional 2.5 percent tariff, which Washington says is linked to forced labour in supply chains.
Critics in Chile argue the tariffs are being used to pressure the government into joining the US-backed Shield of the Americas security alliance.
The alliance is intended to tackle drug trafficking and organised crime, but critics warn it could undermine Chilean sovereignty.
Chile's government has so far resisted joining the alliance, despite pressure from Washington on security and defence policy.

Al Jazeera's Lucia Newman reports from Santiago, Chile.
